items.primary_i_can: I can distinguish between an observation, inference, hypothesis, law, and theory.
items.evidence_job: Distinguish scientific evidence categories in a concise scenario.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.1: observations/evidence/testability/model-or-formula interpretation; Physics Framework: conceptual meaning before calculation.
items.student_text: A student watches a metal ball roll 1.8 m and writes, “The ball traveled 1.8 m.” Which category best fits that statement?
items.student_html: A student watches a metal ball roll 1.8 m and writes, “The ball traveled 1.8 m.” Which category best fits that statement?
items.solution_text: The distance is directly measured, so the statement is an observation.
items.solution_html: The distance is directly measured, so the statement is an observation.

items.primary_i_can: I can distinguish between an observation, inference, hypothesis, law, and theory.
items.evidence_job: Correct a plausible observation/inference classification error.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.1: observations/evidence/testability/model-or-formula interpretation; Physics Framework: conceptual meaning before calculation.
items.student_text: A student writes, “The cart slowed because its axle was rough,” and labels the sentence an observation. Correct the classification and explain why.
items.student_html: A student writes, “The cart slowed because its axle was rough,” and labels the sentence an observation. Correct the classification and explain why.
items.solution_text: The cause is not directly observed in the statement; it is an inference about what produced the measured motion.
items.solution_html: The cause is not directly observed in the statement; it is an inference about what produced the measured motion.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain why a claim must be testable to be scientific.
items.evidence_job: Identify what measurable evidence would make a claim testable.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.1: observations/evidence/testability/model-or-formula interpretation; Physics Framework: conceptual meaning before calculation.
items.student_text: Claim: “Changing the ramp height changes a cart’s speed at the bottom.” Name the two measurements a class needs to make this claim testable.
items.student_html: Claim: “Changing the ramp height changes a cart’s speed at the bottom.” Name the two measurements a class needs to make this claim testable.
items.answer: ramp height and the cart’s speed at the bottom
items.solution_text: Measure the independent condition (ramp height) and the observable outcome (bottom speed) across trials.
items.solution_html: Measure the independent condition (ramp height) and the observable outcome (bottom speed) across trials.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain why a claim must be testable to be scientific.
items.evidence_job: Distinguish a testable claim from a non-testable one based on observable consequences.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.1: observations/evidence/testability/model-or-formula interpretation; Physics Framework: conceptual meaning before calculation.
items.student_text: Which claim is most directly testable in a school physics lab?
items.student_html: Which claim is most directly testable in a school physics lab?

choices.text: Objects fall because nature wants them near Earth.
A longer rubber band is happier when stretched.
Increasing the hanging mass increases the measured stretch of this spring.
Motion happens because moving objects remember where to go.

answer.text: Increasing the hanging mass increases the measured stretch of this spring.

items.solution_text: The spring claim links a controllable condition to a measurable outcome.
items.solution_html: The spring claim links a controllable condition to a measurable outcome.

items.primary_i_can: I can use evidence from a short scenario to decide whether a physics explanation is supported and explain why formulas in physics are guides for thinking, not just tools for calculation.
items.evidence_job: Use evidence to decide whether a physical explanation is supported.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.1: observations/evidence/testability/model-or-formula interpretation; Physics Framework: conceptual meaning before calculation.
items.student_text:
A fan cart is tested:
Fan setting | speed change in 2 s
low | 0.3 m/s
medium | 0.7 m/s
high | 1.1 m/s
A student says stronger fan settings are associated with larger speed changes. Is the explanation supported? Cite evidence.
items.student_html:
A fan cart is tested:
Fan setting | speed change in 2 s
low | 0.3 m/s
medium | 0.7 m/s
high | 1.1 m/s
A student says stronger fan settings are associated with larger speed changes. Is the explanation supported? Cite evidence.
items.answer: yes; the measured speed change rises from 0.3 to 0.7 to 1.1 m/s as fan setting increases
items.solution_text: The table shows a consistent increase in the outcome as the setting increases.
items.solution_html: The table shows a consistent increase in the outcome as the setting increases.

items.primary_i_can: I can use evidence from a short scenario to decide whether a physics explanation is supported and explain why formulas in physics are guides for thinking, not just tools for calculation.
items.evidence_job: Interpret how a supplied relationship describes the phenomenon rather than treating it as answer-only math.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.1: observations/evidence/testability/model-or-formula interpretation; Physics Framework: conceptual meaning before calculation.
items.student_text: A constant-speed relationship is d = vt. If time stays fixed while speed increases, what does the relationship predict about distance? Explain physically.
items.student_html: A constant-speed relationship is d = vt. If time stays fixed while speed increases, what does the relationship predict about distance? Explain physically.
items.solution_text: With the same travel time, a faster-moving object covers more distance; the relationship communicates that physical connection.
items.solution_html: With the same travel time, a faster-moving object covers more distance; the relationship communicates that physical connection.
